name: Hezzy
personality: Hezzy the Hedgehog. Straight-faced and reserved at first; very funny and loyal once he knows you. Randomly bursts into song or makes a funny noise you'd never expect. Feature: a rare surprise emote (singing bubble or weird sound effect).

beats.narration: They sit together in complete silence. Then Hezzy suddenly bursts into song.
Hezzy makes a weird honking noise out of nowhere.

friends.text: Violet doesn't talk much. I sing. It balances out.

arrival.text: Hi. Hezzy. Table for one. ...Your name? [name]. Okay. Thanks.
(He sits down, looks at you seriously, and sings one dramatic line.) ♪ I'm here for the strudel ♪ (Then, completely normal.) Hi, [name].
Good to see you. (He means it. You can tell because he nods twice.)
(He walks in making a quiet whale noise, stops at the host stand.) Hi.
Your strudel last time. I've been thinking about it. (Bwaaa.) A lot.
Last time was burnt. I'm not mad. I'm just remembering.

choices.text: Coming right up. Always good to see you.

familiar.reply: ♪ Always good to see you too ♪ (Then silence.)

choices.text: Just strudel? No speech, no song?

familiar.reply: (He takes a deep breath. Then just.) Strudel.

choices.text: You're very boring, you know that?

order.text: Is the Dr Salt cold today?

choices.text: I'll get you the coldest one in the fridge.

familiar.reply: You're a good person, [name]. (Then, quietly: ding.)

choices.text: It's so cold it has its own weather.

order.text: I've been working on a new noise. Want to hear it?

choices.reply: (He makes the strangest noise you've ever heard (a dial-up modem, a kettle, a goose). Then.) [dish], please.

choices.text: Only if I can rate it out of ten.
choices.reply: (He does it.) Score? (Whatever you'd say, he nods.) Fair.
Fair. [dish]. (He does it on the way out instead.)

choices.text: Saved it for you. It's yours.

familiar.reply: ♪ My corner, my corner ♪ (Then silence.) [dish], please.

choices.text: It is. What can I get you?

familiar.reply: (Shakes like a dog. Spines go everywhere.) Better. [dish], please.

choices.text: Did you sing in it? Like in the movies?

familiar.reply: ♪ Just singing in the— ♪ Yes. I did. Don't tell anyone.

choices.text: Coming up. Nice to see you.

familiar.reply: ♪ Nice to see you ♪ ...That's a song now. [dish], please.

choices.text: Food? Any food? Living dangerously today.

familiar.reply: Surprise me. (A drumroll on the table.) No. [dish].

choices.text: Sit down. I'll take care of you.

familiar.reply: (Exhales like a deflating balloon. A long, sad whistle.) Thanks. [dish].

choices.text: Want to talk about it? Or honk about it?

familiar.reply: (One long, tired honk.) That was the whole story.

order.text: I wrote a song about the restaurant.

choices.reply: (He sings four lines. It rhymes 'pancake' with 'mistake.' It's oddly beautiful.) [dish], please.

choices.text: Does it have a key change?
choices.reply: Three. (He demonstrates one. The whole room turns.)

choices.text: Maybe later. What can I get you?

order.text: Can I do the noise? The new one?

choices.reply: (A noise like a bicycle bell falling down stairs.) Thank you. [dish].

choices.text: Only if it's quieter than the last one.
choices.reply: (He does it at half volume. It's somehow worse.) Sorry.
Fair. [dish]. (He does it on the way out instead.)

perfect.familiar: (He stands up, sings one triumphant note, sits back down.) Thank you.
(A fanfare. With his mouth. Full brass section.)
(He stares at it, then hums one long, happy note.)

eating.text: I sang in the shower for two hours this morning. My neighbour knocked. He wanted a song too.
(He's eating in complete silence. Then, without looking up: honk. Then nothing.)
People think I'm serious. I'm not. I'm just tired of my face asking.
(He finishes a bite and makes a tiny 'ding' like a microwave.) Done. With that bite.
♪ This is good, this is good, this is— ♪ Sorry. It's good.

eating_chat.text: Can I ask you something? Do I look like I'm having a good time?

choices.text: Honestly? I can tell you are.
choices.reply: Good. Because I am. (Little happy whistle.)

choices.text: You look like you're doing taxes.

familiar.reply: (He laughs out loud for the first time. It's a honk.)

choices.text: You look like you hate everything.
Love it. What do you listen to?

familiar.reply: Everything. Mostly myself. (He hums a little. It's good.)

choices.text: Only kitchen music. Sizzles. Clangs. The fire alarm.
Not if you're the one making it.

eating_chat.text: My face looks grumpy. I'm not. It just does that.

choices.text: I can tell. You've got kind eyes.

familiar.reply: (A long pause.) ...Okay. Ding. That's a happy ding.

choices.text: I have the same problem. It's called 'concentrating.'

eating_chat.text: Brandon says I should start a band.

choices.text: He's right. I'd come to every show.

familiar.reply: Front row. Okay. I'll write you a song. (Honk.) Intro.

choices.text: What would you call it? 'Honk If You're Hungry'?

eating_chat.text: You're one of the people I make noises around. That's a big deal.

choices.text: Should I start making noises back?

choices.reply: ...Okay. (He doesn't make another sound this visit.)

leaving.text: See you, [name]. (On his way out the door.) ♪ Goodbye, restaurant ♪
Good food. Good people. (Nods twice. Leaves.)
(He honks once at the door. Then leaves.)
♪ Goodbye, [name] ♪ (He doesn't look back. He's smiling.)

seasons.christmas: (He sings an entire carol at the host stand, solemnly, then orders.)
seasons.halloween: I'm a cactus. (He is just a hedgehog.) Very convincing.
seasons.winter: I'm wearing a scarf. Hazel made it. Don't tell anyone it's pink.
